assumptions: The alignment is correct; the substitution model and rate heterogeneity are as chosen.
Bayesian runs assume a strict clock and the coalescent prior stated.
limits: A tree is an estimate: support values say how well the data pin each clade, and a bootstrap is not a probability of truth.
Heuristic topology search: a better tree may exist.
bio.jane/contract.question: What phylogeny do these aligned sequences support, under a distance, parsimony, maximum-likelihood or Bayesian method, with branch support?

description: Build a phylogeny from aligned sequences — distance methods (NJ, BIONJ, FastME, UPGMA/WPGMA), parsimony, maximum likelihood, or Bayesian MCMC under a strict clock and coalescent prior — with branch support from a bootstrap, aLRT or aBayes, or, for the Bayesian method, clade posterior probabilities. Wire it downstream of align_sequences.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

bayesian_brlen_rate.description: with no clock: rate of the Exponential prior on each branch length (MrBayes brlenspr=unconstrained:exp(rate)); 10 means a prior mean of 0.1 substitutions per site. Only applies when bayesian_clock is none. Advanced.

bayesian_burn_in.description: iterations discarded from the start. Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_chains.description: Metropolis-coupled chains per run (MrBayes nchains; its default is 4): the extra chains sample a flattened posterior and swap states with the cold one, so a run can cross valleys a single chain cannot. Each chain costs a full chain's time. Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_clock.description: clock model: strict (one rate on every branch), ucln, the uncorrelated lognormal relaxed clock (each branch its own rate, mean 1, log-scale sd sampled under Exponential(mean 1/3), as BEAST's UCRelaxedClockModel), or none: an unrooted tree with free branch lengths under an Exponential prior and no coalescent (MrBayes' unconstrained model). Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_clock_sd.description: where the relaxed clock's sigma (log-scale sd of branch rates) starts; always sampled. Only applies when bayesian_clock is ucln. Advanced.

bayesian_gamma_categories.description: discrete-Gamma categories for among-site rate variation (+G, each category its bin mean); 1 is equal rates. Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_iterations.description: Metropolis-Hastings proposals. Each rescores the alignment, so time grows with iterations x taxa x site patterns. Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_kappa.description: transition/transversion ratio for K80/HKY, held fixed. Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_min_part_freq.description: a clade enters the split-frequency deviation only if some run sampled it at least this share of the time (MrBayes minpartfreq). Only applies when method is bayesian. Advanced.

bayesian_model.description: substitution model for the Bayesian chain, its parameters held fixed for the run: base frequencies are the alignment's own for F81/HKY, and kappa is `bayesian_kappa` for K80/HKY. Values: JC69 (JC69), F81 (F81), K80 (K80), HKY (HKY). Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_runs.description: independent runs (MrBayes nruns), seeded seed, seed+1, ...; 2 or more pools their samples and reports the average standard deviation of split frequencies and the PSRF. Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_sample_frequencies.description: sample the base frequencies (F81/HKY) under a flat Dirichlet, starting from the alignment's own. Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_sample_frequency.description: keep one tree every this many iterations after burn-in. Only applies when method is bayesian. Advanced.

bayesian_sample_kappa.description: sample kappa (K80/HKY) under MrBayes' Beta(1,1) prior on kappa/(1+kappa), starting from bayesian_kappa. Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_sample_shape.description: sample the Gamma shape under MrBayes' Exponential(1) prior instead of holding it at bayesian_shape (which becomes the start); needs bayesian_gamma_categories > 1. Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_seed.description: seed of the chain; the same seed and settings reproduce the same samples. Only applies when method is bayesian. Advanced.

bayesian_shape.description: Gamma shape (alpha) for +G, held fixed for the run; smaller means more rate variation among sites. Only applies when method is bayesian.

bayesian_temp.description: heating increment (MrBayes temp): chain j samples the posterior raised to 1/(1 + temp*j). Only applies when method is bayesian. Advanced.

bayesian_theta_prior_mean.description: mean of the Gamma prior on theta = 4N mu, in substitutions per site. Only applies when method is bayesian. Advanced.

bayesian_theta_shape.description: shape of the Gamma prior on theta. Only applies when method is bayesian. Advanced.

bayesian_theta_start.description: starting theta of the chain (not a prior). Only applies when method is bayesian. Advanced.

bootstrap.description: bootstrap replicates; 0 disables. Each replicate rebuilds the whole tree, so cost scales with it — 100 is the conventional minimum for a published tree and is the panel's default. Only applies when support_method is bootstrap.

bootstrap_measure.description: which bootstrap statistic to report. `fbp` is Felsenstein's proportion: the share of replicates that carry this exact branch: a yes/no question per replicate, so one taxon landing elsewhere makes the answer no, which is why a well-supported clade can read near zero on a large tree. `tbe` is the transfer bootstrap expectation (Lemoine et al. 2018, Nature 556:452-456): 1 minus the average number of taxa that would have to move to turn a replicate's nearest branch into this one, over the branch's depth. TBE reads higher than FBP on the same replicates and the two are NOT interchangeable, so say which one a number is. Both read the SAME replicates, so `tbe` costs no extra inference. Only applies when support_method is bootstrap.

bootstrap_seed.description: seed for whichever resampling this run does — the bootstrap's replicates, or SH-aLRT's. The same seed always reproduces the same support values. Only applies when support_method is bootstrap or shalrt. Advanced.

fastme_nni.description: FastME refinement by nearest-neighbour interchange (ape's `nni = TRUE`). Only applies when method is fastme-bal or fastme-ols. Advanced.

fastme_spr.description: FastME balanced refinement by subtree prune-and-regraft (ape's `spr = TRUE`). Only applies when method is fastme-bal. Advanced.

gamma.description: gamma shape for among-site rate variation in the DISTANCE correction; 0 disables. Not the ML +Γ, which is `ml_gamma_categories`. Advanced.

ladderize.description: order each node's children by clade size, so the drawing reads as a ladder. Changes the Newick's child order and nothing about the topology. Advanced.

method.description: tree-building method; distance methods are fast, ML is the slowest and best-justified. Values: nj (Neighbor-Joining), bionj (BIONJ), fastme-bal (FastME (balanced)), fastme-ols (FastME (OLS)), upgma (UPGMA), wpgma (WPGMA), parsimony (Maximum Parsimony), ml (Maximum Likelihood), bayesian (Bayesian (MCMC)).

midpoint_root.description: root the result at its midpoint — a drawing convention, not evidence about where the true root is. Advanced.

ml_gamma_categories.description: discrete-Γ rate categories for the rate heterogeneity across sites; 1 disables it. Only applies when method is ml, or when support_method is alrt or abayes or shalrt. Advanced.

ml_invariant.description: proportion of sites that never change; 0 disables. The starting value when it is estimated. Only applies when method is ml, or when support_method is alrt or abayes or shalrt. Advanced.

ml_model.description: ML substitution model. Values: JC69 (JC69), F81 (F81), K80 (K80), HKY (HKY), TN93 (TN93), GTR (GTR). Only applies when method is ml, or when support_method is alrt or abayes or shalrt. Advanced.

ml_optimise_base_frequencies.description: fit base frequencies rather than holding them equal. Only applies when method is ml. Advanced.

ml_optimise_invariant.description: fit the proportion of invariant sites rather than holding `ml_invariant`. Costs a degree of freedom in AIC/BIC. Only applies when method is ml. Advanced.

ml_optimise_rates.description: fit the substitution rates rather than holding the model's own. Only applies when method is ml. Advanced.

ml_optimise_shape.description: fit the discrete-Γ shape rather than holding `ml_shape`. Costs a degree of freedom in AIC/BIC, and does nothing while `ml_gamma_categories` is 1. Only applies when method is ml. Advanced.

ml_optimise_topology.description: let the ML search move the topology. With this off the result is the Neighbor-Joining topology with ML branch lengths, and the engine says so in a warning. Only applies when method is ml. Advanced.

ml_rearrangement.description: topology search moves for the ML fit. `nni` moves one subtree past its neighbour and stops at the first topology no single move improves, which is a local optimum. `spr` runs that first and then sweeps prune-and-regraft, which reaches trees NNI cannot — at a quadratic number of rearrangements per sweep rather than a linear one. `tbr` runs both and then sweeps tree bisection and reconnection, which cuts a branch and rejoins the two halves by any pair of their branches: the largest neighbourhood here, measured at 1,950 distinct topologies against SPR's 814 on an 18-taxon tree, so roughly 2.4x an SPR sweep. Ignored unless `method` is `ml` and `ml_optimise_topology` is on. Values: nni (NNI), spr (NNI, then SPR), tbr (NNI, then SPR, then TBR). Only applies when method is ml. Advanced.

ml_shape.description: α of the discrete-Γ distribution over site rates — lower means more rate variation between sites. The starting value when the shape is estimated, and the fixed value when it is not. Inert while `ml_gamma_categories` is 1, because one category has no spread. Only applies when method is ml, or when support_method is alrt or abayes or shalrt. Advanced.

model.description: distance/substitution model (ape's names). K80 is the engine's default; very divergent sequences need raw or JC69.

pairwise_deletion.description: exclude a gapped site only from the pairs it is missing in, rather than from every pair. ape's default is off (complete deletion), which keeps distances mutually comparable but discards a column if ANY sequence has a gap there — turn this on for gappy alignments.

parsimony_rearrangement.description: parsimony topology search: `nni` hill-climbs by nearest-neighbour interchange, `spr` adds prune-and-regraft when NNI stalls (phangorn's own default), `tbr` adds bisect-and-reconnect when SPR stalls. Nested, not alternatives: each runs the cheaper moves first, because every NNI move is an SPR move and every SPR move is a TBR move. `tbr` searches the largest neighbourhood this tool offers — 1,950 distinct topologies against SPR's 814 on an 18-taxon tree — and rescores each candidate whole, where SPR scores incrementally, so it is markedly the slowest. Values: nni (Nearest-neighbour interchange), spr (Subtree prune-and-regraft), tbr (Tree bisection and reconnection). Only applies when method is parsimony. Advanced.

sequences.description: aligned sequences — wire align_sequences' rows here, or name library documents.

sh_replicates.description: RELL replicates behind `shalrt` — resamples the three fits' per-site log-likelihoods, not the alignment, so a replicate costs microseconds rather than a whole re-inference. PhyML uses 10,000. Ignored unless `support_method` is `shalrt`. Only applies when support_method is shalrt. Advanced.

support_method.description: which branch support to attach. `bootstrap` resamples alignment columns and rebuilds the tree per replicate (uses `bootstrap`/`bootstrap_seed`). The three branch tests re-infer nothing: they score each internal branch against its two nearest-neighbour rearrangements under the ML model, three likelihood evaluations per branch instead of N whole re-inferences. `alrt` is the parametric test of Anisimova & Gascuel (2006), read against a mixture-of-chi-squares null, and it saturates at 99.985%. `abayes` is the Bayesian support of Anisimova et al. (2011). `shalrt` is the Shimodaira-Hasegawa-corrected variant (PhyML `-b -4`): the same three fits, but the gap is read against a null built by RELL-resampling their per-site log-likelihoods `sh_replicates` times from `bootstrap_seed` — slower than the other two, does not saturate, and usually more conservative. All three use `ml_model`/`ml_gamma_categories`/`ml_shape`/`ml_invariant` for the model, whichever `method` built the tree. Values: bootstrap (Bootstrap), alrt (aLRT), abayes (aBayes), shalrt (SH-aLRT).

name: build_tree

bayesian.description: under `method: bayesian`: the chain (iterations, burn-in, samples, seed, acceptance per operator), the fixed model, the priors, mean / 95% HPD / ESS of log L, theta and root height, every clade's posterior probability (0..1), the commonest topologies and the highest-posterior state. Absent under every other method

branchSupport.description: under `alrt`/`abayes`: the measure, the model, the tree's log-likelihood, and per branch its clade, the two alternative log-likelihoods, the statistic and the support (a fraction, not a percentage). Absent under `bootstrap`

clockDeviationInBranches.description: how far from clock-like the tree is, in MEAN BRANCH LENGTHS. `gamma` and any lineages-through-time reading assume an ultrametric tree; below 1 the raggedness cannot reorder a branching event, above it the statistic is partly rate variation and is not a diversification result

distanceMap.description: that distance matrix as a heatmap

distanceMatrix.description: the pairwise distance matrix the tree was built from

gamma.description: the Pybus-Harvey gamma statistic: negative if branching clusters toward the root (an early burst), positive if toward the tips. A standard normal deviate under the constant-rate null — read it with `gammaP`, and only if `clockDeviationInBranches` is below 1

gammaP.description: two-tailed P for `gamma` against the constant-rate (pure-birth) null

statistics.description: tree statistics: tips, height, total length, diameter, the branch-length distribution, Colless/Sackin imbalance, cherries, treeness, the Pybus-Harvey gamma with its two-tailed P, and the ultrametricity readouts gamma depends on (`isUltrametric`, `rootToTipSpread`, `clockDeviationInBranches`)

transfer.description: under `support_method: bootstrap` with `bootstrap_measure: tbe`: per branch, its clade (the smaller side), its depth, the mean transfer distance over the replicates and the support on 0..1. Absent under `fbp`, which puts its values on the tree and nowhere else

warnings.description: what the method had to say about the data
